name: Traditional/imported eye cosmetics (kohl, surma, kajal) — extreme-Pb platform
anchor: Strictest applicable sovereign FINISHED-COSMETIC contaminant maximum for technically unavoidable heavy-metal impurities, on a total-content basis (ug/kg of product as placed on market). The general tier is anchored by the German BVL 2017 orientation table; the only formulation splits in the family are the German make-up lead and theatrical-make-up arsenic branches and the Korean MFDS nickel product-class tiers, each preserved where the government wrote it. Tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures are anchored on EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75, Appendix 13, an intradermal mixture instrument.
cross_reference: Conventional eye makeup routes to eye-makeup (row 7), which binds a stricter lead value because the German instrument's higher branch does not reach mascara and brow products. Permanent eyeliner routes to tattoo-inks (row 14).
native_basis: finished leave-on cosmetic as placed on market — total heavy-metal content per unit mass of the product as sold (ug/kg). Total content, not a migration or leachate value, and not a dietary basis. No reconstitution, dilution, or in-use concentration conversion is applied: the ceiling is compared to the product in the form the consumer buys it.
native_basis_label: Finished leave-on cosmetic, TOTAL CONTENT as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold), on the technically-unavoidable-impurity basis every instrument in this family uses. Not a migration/leachate basis, not a dietary basis, not an ingredient purity specification.
scope_note: In scope: traditional and imported eye cosmetics of the kohl, kajal, surma, kaajal, al-kahl and tiro type, in powder, paste, stick and pencil form, however marketed, including products sold as eyeliner but formulated on the traditional mineral base. Out of scope: conventional Western eye makeup (row 7) and permanent eyeliner pigment (row 14). This row demands three statements that the numbers alone do not make. First, a PROHIBITION, not a ceiling, is the controlling US restriction: the United States does not list kohl, kajal, al-kahl or surma among the colour additives permitted for cosmetic use, and a cosmetic bearing an unlisted colour additive is adulterated on that basis, so such a product is not lawfully marketable in the United States regardless of its measured lead and a numeric pass on this row is not a marketability finding. HMTc treats an unlawful composition in a target market as a hard stop that no test result cures. Second, the German instrument names 'kajal' expressly in its higher-lead branch at 5000 ug/kg and therefore EXCLUDES this form from its general branch at 2000. That makes 5000 the strictest applicable government value for this row, and the compiler's stricter-unselected audit will surface the 2000 branch: it is inapplicable by the instrument's own scope text, not overlooked. HMTc does not tighten the cell below the government value on precautionary grounds, because Method v2.0 retires precautionary numeric overrides; a lower value has to come from the post-publication certified-lot ratchet under Governance Policy section 12. Third, the honest consequence of that discipline has to be stated rather than hidden: this is the most heavily lead-contaminated cosmetic class in the documented literature, with traditional galena-based and lead-oxide-based preparations reported at percent-level lead, which is four to five orders of magnitude above this row's ceiling. The overwhelming majority of the class fails this standard by orders of magnitude, and the ceiling being 5000 rather than 2000 ug/kg changes nothing about that. The gap between the government value and the toxicological concern for eyelid application in children is real, it is disclosed, and it is not closed by editing the number. The same discipline produces a second uncomfortable result on this row: because every form in it is an eye cosmetic, the Korean eye-makeup nickel branch of 35000 ug/kg applies in full, making this row's nickel ceiling the loosest in the category. That too is the government value and it too is disclosed rather than overridden.
basis_guard: ^(?!.*(color additive ingredient specification|colou?rant impurity|colourant impurity profile|colorant impurity))(?=.*(cosmetic|finished topical product)).*
basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must sit on a FINISHED-COSMETIC (or finished topical product) total-content basis. The guard refuses two families outright. (1) Colour-additive and ingredient purity specifications: the US 21 CFR 73/74 rows, the New Zealand HSR002552 and Singapore ACD carbon-black colourant profiles, the India Cosmetics Rules permitted-colour specification and the Brazil ANVISA RDC 628/2022 organic-colorant specification all bound the purity of ONE raw material, not the maximum for the finished product. Anchoring a finished-product ceiling on a raw-material purity spec is a basis conflation and would be an audit blocker; each of them is also looser than the value that binds here. (2) The EU REACH tattoo and permanent-make-up mixture basis, which is an intradermally introduced mixture and belongs only to the tattoo-inks row. Dietary maximum levels and article migration/extraction limits fail the guard for the same reason.
method: HMTc Method v2.0, government-limit-only initial setting: every numeric cell is the strictest applicable sovereign maximum for this exact leave-on cosmetic form expressed as total content of the finished product as placed on market, or a disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, or a substantiated not-material determination, or a control. No cell is occurrence-derived, no cell is precautionary or feasibility-adjusted, and no cell is anchored on an ingredient or colour-additive purity specification.

Pb.label: Germany BVL 2017: the higher branch of the lead table, 5000 ug/kg, which names kajal expressly and is the exact cell for this product form.
Pb.substantiation: The German lead table has two branches and this form sits in the higher one: it lists 'make-up powder, rouge, eye shadow, eyeliner, kajal, and theater, fan, or carnival make-up' at 5000 ug/kg, and its general branch at 2000 is written 'except listed higher-lead make-up categories', which expressly excludes kajal. The exact cell for this row is therefore regulated at 5000 ug/kg and the general branch is NOT applicable to it. The next applicable instruments are China NMPA 2015, Health Canada and Taiwan MOHW 2024 at 10000, then Korea and Kenya at 20000, so 5000 ug/kg is the strictest applicable sovereign lead maximum for a kohl, kajal or surma product. The compiler's stricter-unselected audit flags the 2000 branch for this row and this substantiation is the record of why it is inapplicable: adopting it would mean asserting that the general branch covers a form its own text excludes. Tightening the cell below the government value on precautionary or occurrence grounds is retired under Method v2.0; the route to a lower value is the certified-lot ratchet. Note the resulting asymmetry plainly: this row's lead ceiling is two and a half times the ceiling on the conventional eye-makeup row, because that row is driven by the unlisted forms (mascara, brow products) that take the general branch. No colour-additive or ingredient purity specification is used as an anchor: the US 21 CFR 73/74 cosmetic-use specifications (10000-20000 ug/kg), the India permitted-colour specification (20000), the Brazil ANVISA RDC 628/2022 organic-colorant specification (20000) and the New Zealand / Singapore carbon-black colourant profiles (10000) bound one raw material's purity rather than the finished product, they are refused by this row's basis guard, and every one of them is looser than the binding value in any event.

Cd.basis: Finished cosmetic total content as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold); technically-unavoidable-impurity basis. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
Cd.label: Strictest applicable sovereign cadmium maximum for a finished cosmetic: Germany BVL 2017 general cosmetic orientation value, 100 ug/kg.
Cd.substantiation: Applicable sovereign maxima surveyed for a finished cosmetic: Germany BVL 2017, 100 ug/kg; Thailand (ASEAN transposition), 3000; Health Canada, 3000; China NMPA 2015, 5000; Taiwan MOHW 2024, 5000; Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, 5000; Singapore HSA 2024 and the ASEAN directive with its Indonesian and Malaysian transpositions, 5000. The German value binds and is 30-fold stricter than the next instrument. Germany writes NO formulation split for cadmium — unlike lead and arsenic, where the same table raises the value for named make-up categories — so the 100 ug/kg value applies to every product form in this category without exception. Sri Lanka SLS 187:2025 (children's skin powder, 3000) carries draft status in the register and is gated out by the compiler.

tAs.basis: Finished cosmetic total content as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold); technically-unavoidable-impurity basis. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
tAs.label: Strictest applicable sovereign total-arsenic maximum for a finished cosmetic: Germany BVL 2017 general cosmetic orientation value, 500 ug/kg.
tAs.substantiation: Applicable sovereign maxima surveyed: Germany BVL 2017 general cosmetic value, 500 ug/kg; China NMPA 2015, 2000; Kenya KS 2937:2021, 2000; Health Canada, 3000; Taiwan MOHW 2024, 3000; Singapore HSA 2024 and the ASEAN directive with its transpositions, 5000; EAEU natural-raw-material tier, 5000; Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, 10000. The German value binds. The only arsenic split the German table writes raises the value to 2500 ug/kg for theatre, fan and carnival make-up, which does not reach this row. The arsenic cells in this instrument family are TOTAL arsenic; no jurisdiction publishes an inorganic-arsenic maximum for a cosmetic, which is why the iAs cell on this row is a control bounded by this total-arsenic ceiling rather than a number.

iAs.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes an inorganic-arsenic maximum for a finished cosmetic. Every instrument in this family regulates TOTAL arsenic, and the register records the family's arsenic rows as tAs for exactly that reason. A total-element ceiling cannot be converted into a species ceiling, species never satisfy totals, and there is no near-neighbour cosmetic inorganic-arsenic cell anywhere to read across from, so no number is invented here. Inorganic arsenic is nevertheless the health-relevant fraction and it is the fraction that travels with the mineral raw materials this category depends on (talc, kaolin, clays, iron oxides, ultramarines, titanium dioxide, zinc oxide), so speciation is mandatory rather than optional.
iAs.reference_method: Arsenic speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS, or an equivalent validated speciation method, on the finished product, reported on the certificate alongside the mandatory total-arsenic result. Inorganic arsenic is bounded above by the published total-arsenic ceiling by identity. Escalation: an inorganic-arsenic result that alone reaches the published total-arsenic ceiling is a hard stop; an inorganic fraction that rises materially against the SKU's own established baseline triggers raw-material traceback and CAPA.

companions.scope: cosmetic products in general except theater, fan, or carnival make-up

tHg.basis: Finished cosmetic total content as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold); technically-unavoidable-impurity basis. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
tHg.label: Strictest applicable sovereign total-mercury maximum for a finished cosmetic: Germany BVL 2017 general cosmetic orientation value, 100 ug/kg.
tHg.substantiation: Applicable sovereign maxima surveyed: Germany BVL 2017, 100 ug/kg; US FDA 21 CFR 700.13 (a binding adulteration rule, mercury unavoidable under good manufacturing practice), 1000; China NMPA 2015, 1000; Health Canada, 1000; Taiwan MOHW 2024, 1000; Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, 1000; Hong Kong Cap. 640, 1000; Singapore HSA 2024 and the ASEAN directive with its transpositions, 1000; Kenya KS 2937:2021, 2000; EAEU TR CU 009/2011 natural-raw-material tier, 1000. The German value binds. The looser mercurial-preservative carve-outs in the register (Hong Kong and India at 70000 ug/kg, South Africa GN R.1227 at 65000 for eye make-up and 30000 for concentrated shampoo or cream, New Zealand HSR002552 at 0.007 percent for eye products) are permissions for the DELIBERATE use of thiomersal or phenylmercuric salts as a preservative. They are not contaminant ceilings, HMTc does not adopt them, and a product relying on an organomercurial preservative is outside this standard.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is a component of total mercury and cannot exceed it by identity, and a leave-on cosmetic matrix supplies no methylation pathway: biotic mercury methylation requires the sulfate- and iron-reducing microbial activity of anoxic aquatic sediment, which has no analogue in an anhydrous, emulsified or preserved cosmetic formulation. Mercury reaches a cosmetic either as an unintentional inorganic trace carried by mineral raw materials or, in the jurisdictions that still permit it, as an organomercurial preservative (thiomersal, phenylmercuric salts) — and neither of those is methylmercury. The published total-mercury ceiling on this row therefore bounds methylmercury completely, so no separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
MeHg.reference_method: No routine methylmercury assay is required. Total mercury by ICP-MS after closed-vessel microwave digestion is mandatory on every lot and bounds methylmercury by identity. Reflex: methylmercury speciation by GC-ICP-MS or an equivalent validated method is required before this determination may be relied on for a lot, wherever the formulation declares a marine-derived, fish-derived or algal-derived ingredient, and for any lot whose total mercury exceeds the published ceiling.
MeHg.substantiation: The determination is bounded, not merely asserted: total mercury is measured on every lot and methylmercury cannot exceed it, so the not-material claim carries a published numeric bound at all times. The marine-, fish- and algal-ingredient reflex closes the only route by which pre-formed methylmercury could enter a cosmetic, which is a contaminated ingredient rather than in-matrix formation.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a methylmercury limit for any cosmetic. Every mercury instrument in this family regulates total mercury: Germany BVL 2017 (100 ug/kg), US FDA 21 CFR 700.13 (1000 ug/kg, calculated as elemental mercury), China NMPA 2015, Health Canada, Taiwan MOHW 2024, Korea MFDS, Hong Kong Cap. 640, the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive with its national transpositions, Kenya KS 2937:2021 and the EAEU technical regulation. The EU prohibits mercury and its compounds as cosmetic ingredients outright under Regulation 1223/2009 Annex II without publishing any speciated value, and the EU tattoo and permanent-make-up restriction likewise sets a total-mercury value only.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU 1223/2009 Annex II; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75 Appendix 13; Germany BVL 2017; US FDA 21 CFR 700.13; Health Canada cosmetic impurity guidance and topical natural-health-product limits; China NMPA 2015; Taiwan MOHW 2024; Korea MFDS Notices 2024-9 and 2025-63; ASEAN Cosmetic Directive 2019 with the Indonesian, Malaysian, Singaporean and Thai transpositions; India Cosmetics Rules 2020 and IS 3959:2004; Kenya KS 2937:2021; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; Hong Kong Cap. 640; New Zealand HSR002552; South Africa GN R.1227. None publishes a methylmercury value for a cosmetic.

Ni.label: Korea MFDS 'eye makeup products' nickel tier, 35000 ug/kg — the branch of the only cosmetic nickel instrument that the government itself writes for this product class.
Ni.substantiation: Korea MFDS is the ONLY authority in the register that publishes a nickel maximum for a finished cosmetic, and the instrument tiers it by product class: eye makeup 35000 ug/kg, colour makeup 30000, all other cosmetics 10000. Method step 4 requires the government's own product-form split to be preserved, so the applicable branch is selected rather than the strictest branch overall. Both register transpositions of the instrument (MFDS Notice 2024-9 and Notice 2025-63) are named and carry identical values, which is the cross-edition check. No other credible authority publishes a cosmetic nickel ceiling: the EU prohibits nickel compounds as intentional cosmetic ingredients under Regulation 1223/2009 Annex II without setting a numeric trace maximum, and Germany's BVL 2017 table covers only lead, cadmium, arsenic, mercury and antimony. Every form in this row — kohl, kajal, surma, kaajal, al-kahl and tiro, in powder, paste, stick and pencil form — is an eye cosmetic applied to the lid margin, so all of them sit inside the Korean eye-makeup product class and the 35000 ug/kg branch is the government's own value for this row; the 10000 'other cosmetics' branch and the 30000 colour-makeup branch are both expressly inapplicable by their own scope text. The compiler's stricter-unselected audit surfaces both and this substantiation is the record of why. The asymmetry is stated plainly rather than left for an auditor to find: this row carries the LOOSEST nickel ceiling in Category 13 while being the most heavily contaminated product class in it, because the Korean government wrote its loosest nickel branch for exactly this product form. Method v2.0 retires precautionary numeric overrides, so HMTc publishes the government value; a tighter nickel value for this row has to come from the post-publication certified-lot ratchet under Governance Policy section 12.

Sn.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes a tin maximum for a finished cosmetic. The register's tin values are dietary maximum levels for canned foods and powdered beverages, and skin-contact-article or food-contact organotin limits — a dietary basis and a migration basis respectively, neither of which can anchor a cosmetic total-content cell — and there is no near-neighbour cosmetic tin cell to read across from. Tin nevertheless enters this category by real routes: tin-oxide pearlescent and nail-lacquer pigments, organotin catalyst and elastomer residues, and tinplate or tin-lined packaging and closures. Testing is therefore mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
Sn.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS after microwave acid digestion, every lot, with organotin speciation by GC-ICP-MS wherever a tin-bearing pigment, catalyst or elastomer component is declared or a tin-lined pack is used. Escalation: a total-tin result above the SKU's established baseline triggers pigment, packaging and closure traceback and CAPA.

Al.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes an aluminium maximum for a finished cosmetic. The register's aluminium values are a food-additive permission (China GB 2760) and a drinking-water guideline, neither of which is a cosmetic total-content basis, and there is no near-neighbour cosmetic aluminium cell to read across from. Aluminium is nonetheless present in this category at high and highly variable levels by design and by mineral origin — alumina and aluminium-hydroxide fillers and substrates, aluminium-lake pigments, kaolin, bentonite and talc, aluminium powder and aluminium salts — so a single contaminant ceiling would be meaningless while the metal itself cannot go unmeasured. Testing is therefore mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-OES or ICP-MS after microwave acid digestion, every lot, reported on the certificate together with the declared aluminium-bearing ingredients so that the measured burden can be reconciled against the formulation. Escalation: an aluminium result that the declared formulation cannot account for triggers raw-material traceback and CAPA, because unexplained aluminium indicates an undeclared mineral filler, which is also the most common carrier of the lead, cadmium and arsenic this row does cap.

Cr.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes a total-chromium maximum for a finished cosmetic. The register's total-chromium values are dietary maximum levels and article limits (toy and stationery coatings, jewellery) in bases that cannot anchor a cosmetic total-content cell, and there is no near-neighbour cosmetic total-chromium cell to read across from. Total chromium in a cosmetic is in any case dominated by benign trivalent chromium from chromium-oxide green and chromium-hydroxide green pigments and from stainless-steel processing contact, so a standalone total-chromium ceiling would not be protective even if a government published one: the health-relevant species is Cr(VI). Total chromium is therefore carried as the mandatory SCREEN that governs the Cr(VI) reflex on this row, and no ceiling is invented.
Cr.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS after microwave acid digestion, every lot. It is the screen, not a pass/fail ceiling. A total-chromium result above the SKU's established baseline, or the declaration of any chromium-bearing pigment, mandates Cr(VI) speciation under this row's Cr-VI control. Escalation: unexplained total-chromium elevation triggers pigment and raw-material traceback and CAPA.

Cr-VI.rationale: No jurisdiction publishes a hexavalent-chromium maximum for a topically applied finished cosmetic. The only Cr(VI) instrument in this instrument family is the EU tattoo and permanent-make-up restriction (REACH Annex XVII entry 75, Appendix 13, 500 ug/kg), which governs a mixture introduced INTRADERMALLY, not a dermal cosmetic; reading it across would substitute one exposure route and one instrument family for another, which is the stretch this method forbids. The remaining sovereign Cr(VI) values in the register are article extraction limits for textiles and leather, a migration basis that cannot anchor a total-content cell. A not-material determination is NOT available here: Cr(VI) in a pigmented cosmetic matrix is not a method artifact, and the EU legislated a Cr(VI) limit for tattoo mixtures precisely because the species occurs in inorganic pigments. The cell is therefore a control.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Hexavalent chromium by alkaline extraction and IC-ICP-MS or an equivalent validated speciation method (EPA 3060A-type digestion), run on every lot alongside the mandatory total-chromium screen. Cr(VI) cannot exceed total chromium by identity. Escalation: any Cr(VI) result above the method reporting limit triggers pigment and raw-material traceback and CAPA; a result at or above 500 ug/kg — cited here as the EU tattoo-mixture escalation reference and expressly NOT as this row's ceiling — is a hard stop pending root-cause closure.
